about: Lesson A19 (a19-gis-siting), 2026-11-06. The map of the region around Prairie City for siting a solar farm, a wind farm, a transmission corridor and a data-center campus. Prairie City is fictional; its numbers are illustrative. Every layer is generated from the seed and the recipe below by assets/learn/components/siting.js (and, the same way, by the lesson's notebook): nothing here was downloaded. Land per MW, setbacks, slope rules and the line cost come from the dated sources listed under sources; every other number is set for teaching and says so. The reference block holds the numbers the page states, computed from the seed by the same code. The data-center campus's size comes from the shared Prairie City data (prairie-city.json), read at run time; the region's geography (districts' extent, river, transmission substations) is this lesson's own.

dataset.creator: Honglin Li
dataset.status: Simulated: every map layer of the fictional region is generated from a seed; land per MW, setbacks, slope rules and the line cost come from dated sources.
dataset.source: Generated by the course's siting code (assets/learn/components/siting.js) from the seed and the recipe in this file.
dataset.license: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), Honglin Li. Values taken from the sources listed in this file keep their publishers' terms; EIA data are U.S. government works in the public domain.

fictional: Prairie City is fictional; its numbers are illustrative.

grid.note: 44 × 30 cells of 1 km × 1 km (1,320 km²); x runs east, y runs south from the north-west corner; each cell is checked for setbacks at 4 × 4 points.

city.name: Prairie City
city.note: Built-up land is where a stretched distance from the center, plus a seeded wobble, is at most 6 km: the core within 2.6 km, the suburbs beyond; the rural fringe district runs out to 9.5 km. Illustrative.

river.name: Prairie River
river.note: The river's center line runs west to east south of the city; the flood zone (standing in for a 1% annual chance flood zone) is 1 to 3 km either side. Illustrative.

slope.note: Mean slope within each cell, in percent: gentle prairie, steeper river bluffs and the flanks of a ridge in the west, a few hills. Illustrative.

wind.note: Mean wind speed at 100 m, m/s: faster to the west and on the ridge. Illustrative, of the size Plains wind maps show.

sun.note: Sunshine as global horizontal irradiance, kWh per m² per day: nearly even across 44 km. Illustrative.

land.note: Land price, dollars per acre (2025 dollars): farmland about $3,000 to $6,000, much more next to the city. Set for teaching.

industrial.name: Industrial park
industrial.note: Food processing and a fertilizer plant; zoned for industry, so a data-center campus may go here but solar and wind farms do not. Illustrative.

homes.note: Farmsteads and fringe homes as points, seeded; the layer is dated 2019. The homes built since then (to 2025) are acreages along the north county road, east of the highway. Illustrative.

substationNote: S1 to S4 are transmission substations on the regional grid, where new plants and large loads connect. They are not the districts' own substations in prairie-city.json (one per district, serving homes and businesses, with their peak-hour limits). Spare capacity (headroom) is the MW a new plant or load could connect at one without an upgrade. Positions and spare capacity are set for teaching.

solar.label: Solar farm
solar.note: 150 MW (AC) of single-axis tracking panels, 1.29 MW of panels (DC) per MW of inverters; arrays need 4.2 acres per MW (DC), so 813 acres, in a 2 km × 2 km block (988 acres) with room for roads and setbacks.

wind.label: Wind farm
wind.note: 150 MW in a 7 km × 7 km block (49 km², 33 ha per MW, near NREL's 34.5 ha per MW average total area); turbines need at least half the block buildable (set for teaching). Land bought: the permanent direct impact, 0.3 ha per MW.

dc.label: Data-center campus
dc.note: Prairie City's campus: its contract, the most it may draw from the grid, is read from prairie-city.json (dataCenter.contractMW) by A19.withCity, never typed here. It builds its own substation, joined by a new line to a transmission substation with that much spare capacity (prairie-city.json: its own substation on the transmission grid, not a district's). Set for teaching here: 0.5 km² (124 acres) of land, a 300 m noise buffer from homes, water from the river or the city's mains, and a road. A data center here is a load and a building, nothing more.

corridor.note: From the wind farm to the nearest substation with 150 MW spare, along the cheapest path over the cost surface; steps between neighboring cells, diagonals included.

deflator.note: Every cost on the page is in 2025 dollars. NREL's line and mitigation costs are 2022 dollars, converted with BEA's GDP implicit price deflator (2017 = 100, annual): × 128.893 / 118.026. The teaching values (access road, water main, land prices) are set in 2025 dollars.

costs.lineNote: Baseline cost of a new 138 kV line per mile, MISO costs (also used for SPP), pastureland, 2022 dollars: NREL's supply curves, Table 11.
costs.multNote: Land-cover multipliers for the same column, NREL's Table 12: pasture or farmland 1.0, suburban 1.1, urban 1.2, wetland 1.8 (used here for the flood zone and the river), hilly 1.1 (used here for slopes above 5%).
costs.mitigationNote: NREL's highest natural and cultural risk mitigation cost, per mile (2022 dollars), used here for a line through protected land when it is allowed.
costs.roadNote: An access road to the nearest paved road, per km, 2025 dollars. Set for teaching.
costs.waterNote: A water main to the river or the city's mains, per km, 2025 dollars. Set for teaching.
costs.solarCF: the region's average sunshine gets EIA's 2025 U.S. utility-scale solar capacity factor (cf_targets.json), and a site's factor scales with its sunshine
costs.windCF: the region's average wind speed gets EIA's 2025 U.S. wind capacity factor (cf_targets.json), plus 7 percentage points per m/s above it (set for teaching)

bea-deflator.text: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, NIPA Table 1.1.9, Implicit Price Deflators for Gross Domestic Product, line 1, annual (2017 = 100): 2022 118.026, 2025 128.893 (read through FRED's annual series A191RD3A086NBEA, BEA the originator, updated 30 September 2026; its 2024 125.587 and 2025 128.893 equal the course's other pages).

lbnl-pv.text: Bolinger, M., and Bolinger, G. (2022). Land Requirements for Utility-Scale PV: An Empirical Update on Power and Energy Density. IEEE Journal of Photovoltaics. Webinar slides, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, 1 February 2022 (PDF): 2019 medians, 4.2 acres per MW (DC) for single-axis tracking arrays, slide 13; DC:AC ratio 1.29 for 2019 tracking plants, slide 8 (the sample table: 66 single-axis tracking plants that came online in 2019, 4,406 MW DC over 3,419 MW AC, the ratio of the year's summed capacities); array area, not the whole site, slide 7.

nrel-pv-2013.text: Ong, S., Campbell, C., Denholm, P., Margolis, R., and Heath, G. (2013). Land-Use Requirements for Solar Power Plants in the United States. NREL/TP-6A20-56290 (PDF): large single-axis PV, total area 8.3 acres per MW (AC), Table ES-1, p. v.

nrel-wind-2009.text: Denholm, P., Hand, M., Jackson, M., and Ong, S. (2009). Land-Use Requirements of Modern Wind Power Plants in the United States. NREL/TP-6A2-45834 (PDF): total area 34.5 ± 22.4 ha per MW; permanent direct impact 0.3 ± 0.3 ha per MW; Table 1, p. 10.

nrel-sc-2024.text: Lopez, A., et al. (2025). Renewable Energy Technical Potential and Supply Curves for the Contiguous United States: 2024 Edition. NREL/TP-6A20-91900, revised June 2025 (PDF): wind siting, Table 7, pp. 20–23 (structure setback 220 m reference, 400 m limited; slope above 25% or 13%); solar siting, Table 9, pp. 26–29 (building setback 61 m or 152 m; slope above 10% or 5%); reference = the median of existing local ordinances, limited = the 90th percentile, p. 19; transmission by least-cost path, §2.5; Tables 11 and 12 and the mitigation costs, p. 34.

reference.note: Computed from the seed by the page's model; the lesson's notebook rebuilds these numbers from the seed and checks them.

cityDataCenter.from: prairie-city.json, dataCenter.contractMW (copied here, so the notebook needs only this file)
